result_text:
Per-extension entries are now named by the bare lower-cased extension (`"java"`, `"js"`, `"xml"`). Tests pass in `codeanalyzer` (336 run, 0 failures, 3 skipped) and `reports` (all passing). I didn't add a test for the mixed old/new landscape merge, so that path is untested.

- **Naming:** `SourceCodeAspectUtils.getAspectsPerExtensions` creates aspects named by the bare extension instead of `"  *." + extension`. This is what ends up in `linesOfCodePerExtension` and `fileCountPerExtension` in `analysisResults.json`.
- **Metric ids and summary:** In `AnalysisUtils` the metric ids come out unchanged (`LINES_OF_CODE_MAIN_EXT_JAVA` and so on). The `  *.ext: N files, …` summary lines keep their look because the decoration is added back when the line is printed.
- **Landscape merge:** In `LandscapeAnalysisResults` a new `normalizeExtensionName` helper trims, lower-cases and strips a leading `*.`. It is applied when merging repositories and when merging the "other" category (build and deployment, generated, other). `"  *.java"` and `"java"` therefore land in one `"java"` entry, and its per-repository breakdown lists every contributing repository.
- **Tests:** `CodeConfigurationTest` and `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest` now assert the bare names.

I left the existing `.replace("*.", "")` calls in the report code alone. They do nothing on bare names and still clean up old data.
